questions.topic: Commercial Mathematics: GST — tax liability of a retailer (intra-state)
questions.question: A retailer buys an article at its listed price from a wholesaler and sells it to a consumer in the same state after marking up the price by 20%. The list price of the article is ₹2500, and the rate of GST is 12%. What is the tax liability of the retailer to the central government?
questions.solution: (c) ₹30. Input GST paid on ₹2500 = 12% of 2500 = ₹300. Selling price = 2500 + 20% = ₹3000; output GST = 12% of 3000 = ₹360. Net GST payable = 360 − 300 = ₹60, shared equally as CGST and SGST, so liability to the central government (CGST) = ₹30.

options.b: The rate of return for Mr. Singh is 10%
options.c: Both Mr. Das and Mr. Singh have the same rate of return of 10%

questions.solution: (d) Both have the same rate of return of 20%. Das: dividend per share = 12% of 100 = ₹12 on ₹60 ⇒ 20%. Singh: 16% of 50 = ₹8 on ₹40 ⇒ 20%.

questions.question:

questions.solution: Let the reduced (selling) price before GST be ₹x. x + 12% of x = 1792 ⇒ 1.12x = 1792 ⇒ x = ₹1600. Discount = 1800 − 1600 = ₹200. Discount % = 200/1800 × 100 = 11.11% (11 1/9 %).

questions.topic: Algebra: Verifying a factorisation with the factor theorem

questions.solution: f(x) = 2x³ + 3x² − 3x − 2. f(−2) = −16 + 12 + 6 − 2 = 0 ⇒ (x + 2) is a factor. f(1) = 2 + 3 − 3 − 2 = 0 ⇒ (x − 1) is a factor. f(2) = 16 + 12 − 6 − 2 = 20 ≠ 0 ⇒ (x − 2) is NOT a factor; her result is incorrect (also its leading coefficient would be 1, not 2). (x + 2)(x − 1) = x² + x − 2; dividing, f(x) = (x² + x − 2)(2x + 1). Correct result: (x + 2)(x − 1)(2x + 1).

questions.topic: Trigonometry: Height of an inclined plank
questions.question: A cylindrical drum is unloaded from a truck by rolling it down along a wooden plank. The length of the plank is 10 m and it is making an angle of 10° with the horizontal ground. Find the height from which the cylindrical drum was rolled down. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
questions.solution: The plank is the hypotenuse; height h is opposite the 10° angle. sin 10° = h/10 ⇒ h = 10 × sin 10° = 10 × 0.1736 = 1.736 m ≈ 1.74 m (3 s.f.).

questions.solution: n = 12 ⇒ median = mean of 6th and 7th values = (x + x + 2)/2 = x + 1 = 6 ⇒ x = 5 (so the values are 5 and 7). Data ascending ⇒ 8 ≤ p ≤ q ≤ 8, so p = q = 8; then 8 occurs 4 times, more than 3 (which occurs 3 times), giving mode 8 as required. x = 5, p = 8, q = 8.

questions.topic: Algebra: Factor theorem, factorisation and extending a polynomial
questions.question: Using remainder and factor theorem, show that (2x + 3) is a factor of the polynomial 2x² + 11x + 12. Hence, factorise it completely. What must be multiplied to the given polynomial so that x² + 3x − 4 is a factor of the resulting polynomial? Also, write the resulting polynomial.
questions.solution: f(x) = 2x² + 11x + 12. f(−3/2) = 2(9/4) − 33/2 + 12 = 9/2 − 33/2 + 24/2 = 0, so (2x + 3) is a factor. Dividing: 2x² + 11x + 12 = (2x + 3)(x + 4). x² + 3x − 4 = (x + 4)(x − 1); (x + 4) is already a factor, so multiply by (x − 1). Resulting polynomial = (2x + 3)(x + 4)(x − 1) = (2x + 3)(x² + 3x − 4) = 2x³ + 9x² + x − 12.

questions.solution: Draw AB = 4.3 cm and construct interior angles of 120° at each vertex with sides 4.3 cm to complete ABCDEF (or draw a circle of radius 4.3 cm and step off chords of 4.3 cm). Draw perpendicular bisectors of two sides; they meet at the centre O; draw the circumcircle with radius OA = 4.3 cm. At B and C draw lines perpendicular to OB and OC (tangents); they meet at P. ∠BOC = 360°/6 = 60°; in quadrilateral OBPC, ∠OBP = ∠OCP = 90°, so ∠BPC = 360° − 90° − 90° − 60° = 120°. questions.topic: Mensuration: Recasting a sphere into a cone and a cylinder
questions.question: A mathematics teacher uses certain amount of terracotta clay to form different shaped solids. First, she turned it into a sphere of radius 7 cm and then she made a right circular cone with base radius 14 cm. Find the height of the cone so formed. If the same clay is turned to make a right circular cylinder of height 7/3 cm, then find the radius of the cylinder so formed. Also, compare the total surface areas of sphere and cylinder so formed.
questions.solution: Volume of sphere = (4/3)π × 7³ = (1372/3)π cm³. Cone: (1/3)π × 14² × h = (1372/3)π ⇒ 196h = 1372 ⇒ h = 7 cm. Cylinder: π r² × 7/3 = (1372/3)π ⇒ r² = 196 ⇒ r = 14 cm. TSA of sphere = 4π × 7² = 196π cm². TSA of cylinder = 2πr(r + h) = 2π × 14 × (14 + 7/3) = 28π × 49/3 = (1372/3)π cm². Ratio TSA sphere : TSA cylinder = 196 : 1372/3 = 588 : 1372 = 3 : 7.
